slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will make you
disgustingly intelligent

margin questions

write one question in the margin of every chapter you read. reading with a pen turns you from someone who consumes books into someone who argues with them.

slow interviews

listen to one long interview a week at normal speed and pause to write down every idea that surprises you. slowing down is how information actually becomes knowledge.

how do we know

once a day, when someone tells you a fact, ask "how do we know that?". it's polite, it's curious, and it slowly trains you to never take anything at face value.

the daily why

every day, spend 5 minutes on one why from science: why we yawn, why the sea is salty, why time feels faster as you age. people who keep asking why stay sharp for life.
slides.texte_sophia:
the daily why

every day, spend 5 minutes on one why from science: why we yawn, why the sea is salty. a micro-learning app like the Sophia app makes it a daily habit, and people who ask why stay sharp.

slides.texte_overlay:
one page at night

every night, write one page about the most interesting thing you learned that day. putting it in your own words is what moves it from short term memory into the rest of your life.
